plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/23185
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). Template tag is Social-ext-Phish, but the sources describe a long pretext (fake trading firm, in-person conference meetings, Telegram), not phishing email, so Social variety Pretexting with vectors In-person and IM; target Developer/contributors. Malware is coded with variety Unknown because Drift suspects a shared code repository and a TestFlight app infected contributor devices (not confirmed, no family named). The final drain step is coded hacking Unknown: The Hacker News' earlier headline mentions 'durable nonce' transactions, but the article read gives no detail.
Actor: Drift attributes with medium confidence to DPRK UNC4736 (AppleJeus, Citrine Sleet, Golden Chollima) -> Nation-state KP, Financial.
Data/impact: $285M -> Virtual currency, impact. Asset S - Other = protocol contracts/vaults on Solana.
Timeline: operation began fall 2025 (month not given) -> incident year 2025 only; theft April 1 2026 -> compromise about 6 months. dbir_year 2027 is derived from the theft date (the later, precise anchor) since 'fall 2025' could fall either side of the Nov 1 cutoff.
Discovery: internal Incident response (Drift's device review traced it back to the trading group). Victim country/headcount Unknown; NAICS 523999 from the issue.

event_chain.summary: Pretext as quant trading firm builds trust with contributors
Contributor devices likely infected via shared repo/app
Steps to obtain control not documented

summary: On April 1, 2026 Solana-based decentralized exchange Drift lost about $285 million in a theft that Drift says capped a six-month social engineering operation by North Korea-linked UNC4736 (AppleJeus/Citrine Sleet). Starting in fall 2025, operatives posing as a quantitative trading firm met Drift contributors at conferences, built a relationship over Telegram, deposited $1 million and discussed vault integrations. Drift believes contributors' devices were compromised through a shared code repository and a possibly malicious TestFlight app, leading to the theft.
